known_issue_dedup_ineffective.summary: Alert dedup cannot work as configured. Each scheduled run executes on its own fresh branch and commits last_snapshot.json / today_alerts.json only to that branch. main has never carried these files, so a run that reads only its own checkout starts with no prior alert log and no prior snapshot to diff against.
known_issue_dedup_ineffective.observed_impact: On 2026-08-22, 8 near-identical SPUS concentration alert emails were delivered hourly (01:20, 03:20, 07:21, 08:21, 09:20, 11:20, 12:20, 15:20 UTC). Each run re-derived the same standing breach with an empty today_alerts.json.
known_issue_dedup_ineffective.current_mitigation: The SPUS concentration-check exclusion added to st0ck_rules.md at 2026-08-22 15:23 UTC suppresses that specific alert at the source. All runs on 2026-08-24 have logged 0 alerts.
known_issue_dedup_ineffective.workaround_used_this_run: Recovered prior state by scanning all remote claude/* branches and reading last_snapshot.json / today_alerts.json from the most recently committed one (claude/brave-fermi-lbs0g1, 15:24 UTC), then carried today's full run history forward into this file.
known_issue_dedup_ineffective.residual_risk: Dedup remains structurally non-functional for any genuine future trigger (a real -15%/-20% cost breach, a >=5% intraday move, or a non-SPUS weight breach). Such an alert would re-send on every hourly run for the rest of the day unless the run happens to perform the cross-branch recovery above.
known_issue_dedup_ineffective.suggested_fix: Persist last_snapshot.json and today_alerts.json to main (or one stable state branch) that every run reads and writes, instead of a per-run branch. Not actioned here: this session is restricted to pushing to claude/brave-fermi-n056m2 and has no permission to push to main.
